claims.text: A Secret is an object similar to a ConfigMap but intended for confidential data such as passwords; values under data are base64-encoded strings.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Configuration > Secrets (overview; data field base64-encoded)

claims.text: secretKeyRef under env[].valueFrom sets one environment variable from one key of a named Secret; the value is set when the container starts (like ConfigMap env).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Secrets (Using Secrets as environment variables: env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef)

claims.text: base64 is an encoding, not encryption: base64 -d recovers the original bytes without any key.
claims.source_hint: RFC 4648; kubernetes.io Secrets ('base64 encoded; it is obscured but not secret'); outputs secrets.txt

claims.text: By default, Secrets are stored unencrypted in etcd by the API server; encryption at rest must be configured by a cluster administrator.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Secrets (caution: stored unencrypted in etcd by default; Enable Encryption at Rest)

claims.text: kubectl describe secret prints only the size in bytes of each data key, not the values.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Managing Secrets using kubectl (describe shows 'password: 12 bytes'); outputs secrets.txt

claims.text: Anyone allowed to read a Secret through the API server can retrieve its data (kubectl get secret -o jsonpath) and decode it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Secrets caution ('Anyone with API access can retrieve or modify a Secret'); outputs secrets.txt

claims.source_hint: kubectl create secret generic reference (--dry-run=client, -o yaml); kubectl apply reference

claims.text: Who can get a Secret's value: anyone allowed to read it through the API server, anyone with access to etcd, and anyone allowed to create Pods in its namespace (a Pod can take any Secret there as env).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Secrets caution ('anyone who is authorized to create a Pod in a namespace can use that access to read any Secret')

claims.text: The kubelet fetches the Secret and sets the env value from secretKeyRef when it starts the container.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Secrets (Using a Secret; 'If the Secret cannot be fetched ... the kubelet periodically retries')

claims.text: Read permission can be granted per kind of object (resource type), so a cluster can allow reading ConfigMaps in a namespace without allowing reading Secrets.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Using RBAC Authorization (rules list resources such as configmaps, secrets)

claims.text: kubectl create secret generic creates a Secret of type Opaque with arbitrary keys; each --from-literal=KEY=value adds one key; -o jsonpath='{.data.KEY}' prints that key's base64 value.
claims.source_hint: kubectl create secret generic reference; kubernetes.io Secrets (Opaque secrets); kubectl JSONPath support
